quda_coarse_precision.semantics: fine c128 solve with double coarse MG fields

reference_solver.timing_semantics: same caller-owned input/output and true-residual gate; outside MultiGrid and excluded from speedup

fused_workspace_terms.B_f: one compact fine-parity vector in bytes
fused_workspace_terms.B_c: one full first-coarse-level vector in bytes

protocol.initial_guess: zero for every warmup and measured solve

timing_contract.setup: host inputs -> gauge/clover/runtime ready; includes cache lookup/restore, excludes cache persistence
timing_contract.cache_lookup_or_restore: reported as a disjoint setup component
timing_contract.cache_persist: reported separately and excluded from setup total
timing_contract.steady_solve: zero-x0 solve call bracketed by CUDA synchronization
timing_contract.true_residual: computed after each timed solve and excluded from solve time
timing_contract.first_solve_memory: the first zero-x0 warmup is sampled for lazy solver/workspace allocation; excluded from warmup/repeat timing statistics
timing_contract.memory_probe: one additional post-timing solve with 10 ms device-wide cudaMemGetInfo sampling; excluded from warmups/repeats/statistics

residual_contract.operator: full periodic Wilson+Clover, csw=1, PyQCU normalization

null_vectors.parity: full (even reconstructed once; odd copied verbatim)

quda.iteration_semantics: finest total_iterations is the outer GCR total; smoother and coarse iterations are separate per-level counters
quda.iteration_scope: outer GCR iterations; recursive MG and coarse solver iterations are recorded separately in QUDA_MG_TRACE

krylov.note: QUDA native workspace is not exposed by PyQUDA

timing_boundary.detail: low-level invertQuda writes the caller-owned output
timing_boundary.performance_call: omitted; no high-level allocation/performance call in timer
